about: The third part of text ga, the bardo of the wrathful deities: day twelve and the first of the wrathful goddesses. Those who, for all the pointing out, are drawn back by bad habits and flee in terror meet, on the twelfth day, the blood-drinkers of the karma family with the Gaurīs, the Phra men and the Īśvarīs. Karma Heruka, dark green, with three faces, six arms and four legs spread wide, holding a sword, a khaṭvāṅga, a staff, a bell, a skull-cup and a plough, embraced by his consort Karmakrodhīśvarī, dawns from the north of the dead person's own brain. He is not to be feared: he is the dead person's own yidam, and in truth Amoghasiddhi, and to recognise him is to be freed. The text explains why this works: as a man who is told that a lion is only a stuffed one loses his fear, so one who has the lama's instruction knows the huge blood-drinkers for his own appearance, and the clear light taught before and the clear light that dawns now meet like mother and child. Then come, each from a quarter of the brain and each with her colour and what she holds, the eight Gaurīs of the sacred places, the eight Phra men of the lands with the heads of lion, tiger, fox, wolf, vulture, charnel bird, crow and owl, the four gatekeepers with the heads of tiger, sow, lion and snake, and, in the outer ring of the thirty deities of the fierce heruka, the twenty-eight Īśvarīs with their many heads and weapons, of whom the six yoginīs of the east are described here. Again and again the dead person is told not to fear them and to recognise whatever dawns as his own appearance, the energy of awareness.

sentences.w: ཡང་ དེ་ལྟར་ ངོ་སྤྲད་ ཀྱང་ བག་ཆགས་ ངན་པས་ ཕྱིར་ ཁྲིད་ དེ་ དངངས་སྐྲག་ སྐྱེས་ ནས་ བྲོས་པས་ ཡི་དམ་དུ་ ངོ་ མ་ ཤེས་ ཏེ་ མ་ འཕྲོད་པ་ ཡོད་པས༔
sentences.l: Again, thus face-introduced though, habitual-tendencies bad-by back led, and, terror-fright arisen, then, fled-because, yidam-as face not knowing, and, not meeting there-are-because:
sentences.i: But even when pointed out in this way, some are drawn back by bad habitual tendencies, are struck with terror and fright and flee; and because there are those who do not know them as their yidam and do not recognise,
sentences.n: The part begins on the line where 010 ended, after the eleventh day. ngo sprad kyang, 'though pointed out' (sprad, the past of sprod). bag chags ngan pas, 'by bad habitual tendencies', with -s, 'by'. phyir khrid de, 'is led back, drawn away': khrid is the past stem of 'khrid, 'to lead'; de is the form of ste after -d. dngangs skrag skyes nas, bros pas: the words of the days before. ngo ma shes te ma 'phrod pa yod pas, 'because there are (those) who do not know and do not meet': yod pa, 'there being', with -s, 'because', runs on to the next sentence. The other recension has ngo ma 'phrod pa srid pas, 'because it can happen that they do not recognise'; the print says the same in more words.

sentences.w: ཡང་ ཞག་ བཅུ་གཉིས་པ་ ལ་ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ ལས་ ཀྱི་ རིགས་ ཀྱི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ དང༔ གོའུ་རི་མ་ དང༔ ཕྲ་མེན་ དང༔ སྨེ་མ་ དང༔ དབང་ཕྱུག་མ་ རྣམས་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ འོང་ སྟེ༔ ངོ་ མ་ ཤེས་པར་ འཇིགས་སྐྲག་ ཆེ་རུ་ འོངས་པས༔
sentences.l: Again, day twelfth on, blood-drinking karma family's deity-host and, Gaurīs and, Phra-men and, Sme-ma and, Īśvarīs (plural) welcoming for come, and: face not knowing-ly, terror-fright great-to came-because:
sentences.i: on the twelfth day the host of blood-drinking deities of the karma family, with the Gaurīs, the Phra men, the Sme ma and the Īśvarīs, comes to meet him; and because he does not recognise them, his terror and fright grow great.
sentences.n: zhag bcu gnyis pa, 'the twelfth day' (bcu gnyis, 'ten-two'). las kyi rigs, 'the family of action' (las, 'deed, karma'), the family of Amoghasiddhi, the buddha of the fifth day. Here the goddesses who stand round the five blood-drinkers are named in classes, each with dang, 'and'. go'u ri ma, Sanskrit Gaurī in Tibetan letters with the feminine -ma; below the print also writes ga'u ri. phra men, a Tibetan name for the animal-headed goddesses who follow the Gaurīs; its origin is not explained in the text. dbang phyug ma, 'Lady' (dbang phyug, 'lord', Sanskrit īśvara, with -ma), the Īśvarīs who come last. sme ma is not explained: it may stand for the goddesses of the charnel ground, like Śmaśānī below, or for the four gatekeepers, who are otherwise missing from the list; the other recension has no sme ma and has phra men ma. bsu ba la 'ong, 'come to welcome'. che ru 'ongs pas, 'because (the fear) has come to be great': ru, 'to', after a vowel; 'ongs, the past stem of 'ong, 'to come'. The other recension has ngo mi shes par skrag tu 'ong bas, 'because, not recognising, they come to be afraid'.

sentences.w: ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ ནི༔ ཡང་ ཚེ་འདས་ ཀྱི་ མིང་ ནས་ བོད་ ལ་ འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱེ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔
sentences.l: The face-introduction, as-for: again, the dead-one's by-name called(?), and, these-words: O child-of-noble-family!
sentences.i: This is how he is pointed out. Again call the dead person by name and say this: O child of noble family,
sentences.n: The formula of the days before, but the print has bod la where it has bos la everywhere else, and again below (101.5): bos is the past stem of 'bod, 'to call'. The da is clear on the image; bod may be the print's spelling of 'bod without its prefix, or of the future bod, so it is kept and read 'call'. The reading is not certain enough to correct. The print has no ma yengs par nyon cig, 'listen without distraction', which the other recension has here. The print runs ming and nas together across the line join and the ornament of the leaf front, here divided.

sentences.w: ཞག་ བཅུ་གཉིས་ སོང་བའི་ དུས་སུ༔ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ ལས་ ཀྱི་ རིགས་ ཀྱི་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ ཀརྨ་ཧེ་རུ་ཀ་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ༔ སྐུ་མདོག་ ལྗང་ནག་ ཞལ་ གསུམ་ ཕྱག་ དྲུག་ ཞབས་ བཞི་ བགྲད་པ༔ ཞལ་ གཡས་ དཀར་བ༔ གཡོན་ དམར་བ༔ དབུས་ ལྗང་ནག་ ཇམས་པ༔
sentences.l: Days twelve gone's time-at, blood-drinking karma family's Blessed-One Karma-Heruka so-called, body-colour dark-green, faces three, hands six, feet four spread-wide; face right white, left red, centre dark-green fierce(?);
sentences.i: when twelve days have passed, the blood-drinking Blessed One of the karma family, called Karma Heruka, dark green in colour, with three faces, six arms and four legs spread wide, his right face white, his left red, his centre one dark green and fierce(?),
sentences.n: song ba'i dus su, 'at the time when (twelve days) have gone' (song, the past of 'gro, 'to go'). Karma he ru ka, Sanskrit in Tibetan letters, Karma Heruka, 'the heruka of the karma family'; the other recension writes karmā. ljang nag, 'dark green' (ljang, 'green'; nag, 'black'), the colour of the karma family. The description runs as on the days before. jams pa: the letter is clearly ja on the image, but jams gives no sense here; the sense wants 'fierce', rngam pa, which the other recension has, and ja for rnga may be an error in cutting the block. It is kept as printed and read 'fierce(?)'. The print runs dbus and ljang together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: ཕྱག་ དྲུག་ གཡས་ ཀྱི་ དང་པོ་ ན་ རལ་གྲི༔ བར་པ་ ན་ ཁ་ཊྭཾ་ག༔ ཐ་མ་ ན་ དབྱུག་ཏོ༔ གཡོན་ གྱི་ དང་པོ་ ན་ དྲིལ་བུ༔ བར་པ་ ན་ བྷནྡྷ༔ ཐ་མ་ ན་ མཐོང་གཤོལ་ བསྣམས་པ༔
sentences.l: Hands six, right's first in sword; middle in khaṭvāṅga; last in staff; left's first in bell; middle in skull-cup; last in plough holding;
sentences.i: in his six hands, on the right, the first holds a sword, the middle a khaṭvāṅga, the last a staff; on the left, the first a bell, the middle a skull-cup, the last a plough;
sentences.n: The six implements are counted as on the days before. ral gri, 'sword'; kha TwaM ga, the khaṭvāṅga, the staff topped with skulls, in three syllables as on the eleventh day; dbyug to, 'staff'; dril bu, 'bell'. bhandha is the skull-cup, written here in one syllable with the letters stacked (བྷནྡྷ), where 010 mostly has bhan dha in two; the sense is the same. mthong gshol is the print's spelling of thong gshol, 'plough', which the other recension has, with a ma added at the front as in 010 (mthong shol). bsnams pa, 'holding', the respectful word.

sentences.w: ཡུམ་ ཀརྨ་ཀྲོ་ཏི་ཤྭ་རི་མ་ སྐུ་ ལ་ འཁྲིལ་བ༔ གཡས་པས་ ཡབ་ ཀྱི་ མགུལ་ ནས་ འཁྱུད་པ༔ གཡོན་པས་ དུང་ དམར་ ཞལ་དུ་ སྟོབ་པ༔
sentences.l: The mother Karmakrodhīśvarī body to embracing; right-by father's neck at embracing; left-by conch red mouth-to feeding;
sentences.i: his consort Karmakrodhīśvarī embraces his body: with her right hand she holds the father round the neck, and with her left she puts a red conch to his mouth;
sentences.n: Karmakrodhīśvarī, 'Wrathful Lady of the karma family', with kro ti for krodhī as before; the other recension writes kro tu. yab kyi mgul nas, 'at the father's neck': the print names the father here, where the days before had mgul alone; the other recension has yab kyi both here and in yab kyi sku la, 'the father's body', and the print has sku la alone. 'khyud pa, 'embracing', closes the phrase with -pa, where the days before had 'khyud cing, 'embraces, and'.

sentences.w: ཡབ་ཡུམ་ ཞལ་སྦྱོར་དུ་ མངོན་སུམ་དུ་ རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ བྱང་ ནས་ ཐོན་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ འཆར་རོ༔
sentences.l: Father-mother face-joining-in, manifest-ly, own's brain's north from emerged, then, oneself to dawns.
sentences.i: Father and mother in union come out of the north of your own brain and dawn before you, plainly before your eyes.
sentences.n: zhal sbyor du, 'in union', with -du, where the eleventh day had zhal sbyor alone. byang nas, 'from the north', the quarter of the karma family. The other recension has klad pa'i nang gi byang nas, 'from the north within the brain'. 'char ro, 'dawns', with the sentence-ending -o after -r.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔ མ་ སྐྲག་ཅིག༔ མ་ དངངས་ཤིག༔ རང་ གི་ རིག་པའི་ སྐུར་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Him at not fear! Not be-afraid! Not be-terrified! Own's knowing's body-as face-knowing do!
sentences.i: Do not fear him. Do not be afraid. Do not be terrified. Recognise him as the form of your own awareness.
sentences.n: The three commands and the call to recognise, as on the eighth day (010); dngangs is the print's spelling of sngangs, which the other recension has.

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ ཡི་དམ་ གྱི་ ལྷ་ ཡིན་པས་ མ་ སྐྲག་ཅིག༔ དོན་ ལ་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ དོན་ཡོད་གྲུབ་པ་ དངོས་ ཡིན་ནོ༔ མོས་པ་ དང་ གུས་པ་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔ ངོ་ ཤེས་པ་ དང་ གྲོལ་བ་ མཉམ་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: You-yourself's yidam's deity is-because, not be-afraid! Meaning-in, the Blessed-One Amoghasiddhi itself is. Devotion and respect do! Face-knowing and freeing together comes.
sentences.i: He is your own yidam deity, so do not be afraid. In truth he is the Blessed One Amoghasiddhi himself. Have devotion and respect. Recognising and freedom come together.
sentences.n: Karma Heruka is Amoghasiddhi (Don yod grub pa, 'He Whose Aim Is Accomplished'), the buddha of the fifth day. Here the print has no yab yum, 'with his consort', which it has on the days before and the other recension has here, and closes the sentence with yin no, 'he is', where the days before had yin pas, 'because he is', running on to the command that follows ('so do not fear' on the eighth day, 'so have devotion' on the tenth and eleventh); here mos pa dang gus pa gyis shig stands as a sentence of its own. mos pa dang gus pa, 'devotion and respect' (gus pa, 'respect, reverence'); the other recension adds dung dung, 'intensely, with longing'. mnyam du 'ong ngo, 'come together', where the days before had dus mnyam du, 'at the same time'.

sentences.w: ཞེས་ བསྒྲགས་པས་ ཡི་དམ་དུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ ནས་ གཉིས་སུ་ མེད་པར་ ཐིམ་ ནས་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: So proclaimed-because: yidam-as face-knowing, then, two-as without-ly dissolving, then, buddha becomes.
sentences.i: When this is proclaimed, he recognises him as his yidam, dissolves into him without duality, and becomes a buddha.
sentences.n: As on the ninth and tenth days (010).

sentences.w: དེ་ དག་ བླ་མའི་ གདམས་ངག་ གི་ རང་སྣང་ རིག་པའི་ རྩལ་དུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པས༔ དཔེར་ན་ སེང་གེའི་ གསོབ་ མཐོང་བར་ ལྟ་བུར་ གྲོལ་ལོ༔
sentences.l: Those, lama's instruction by(?), self-appearance, knowing's energy-as face-knowing-because: for-example, lion's stuffed-one seeing-as like, freed.
sentences.i: By the lama's instruction they recognise these deities as their own appearance, the energy of awareness, and so they are freed, as when one sees that a lion is only a stuffed one.
sentences.n: de dag, 'those', the deities just described. gi, 'of', is read as gis, 'by', which the other recension has (as with kyi for kyis in 010). rang snang, 'self-appearance', what the mind itself shows. rtsal, 'skill, energy, play', the power of awareness to show itself as forms; rtsal is doubtful on the image ([?]), though the other recension has it and the print has rig pa'i rtsal du clearly at 105.1. dper na, 'for example'. seng ge'i gsob, 'a stuffed lion, a dummy lion' (seng ge, 'lion'; gsob, 'hollow, stuffed, sham'): a lion's skin stuffed with straw, which frightens until one sees what it is. mthong bar lta bur, 'like seeing' (lta bu, 'like', with -r), where the other recension has mthong ba lta bur. grol lo, 'are freed', closes the sentence; the other recension runs on with grol te.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ སེང་གེའི་ གསོབ་ འདི་ལྟར་ ཡིན་ གྱི།། དོན་ མ་ རྟོགས་ ན་ དངངས་སྐྲག་ སྐྱེས་ ཏེ༔ མི་ གཅིག་ གིས་ འདི་ལྟར་ ཡིན་ གྱི་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པས་ མཚང་ རིགས་ ཏེ་ འཇིགས་པ་ བྲལ་བ་ འདྲ་བར༔
sentences.l: That also: lion's stuffed-one, thus is, but: meaning not understood if, terror-fright arises, and: person one by 'thus it-is' gyi(?) face-introduced-because, the-secret seen, and, fear freed-of alike-ly:
sentences.i: It is like this: a stuffed lion is only what it is, but if one does not see the point, terror and fright arise; and when someone points out to one that this is all it is, one sees through it and is rid of fear. In the same way,
sentences.n: de yang, 'that is to say', opens the explanation of the example. 'di ltar yin gyi, 'it is (only) like this, but': gyi after a verb marks a contrast, 'it is so, but (one does not see it)'. The print closes the phrase with the plain double stroke །། instead of ༔. don ma rtogs na, 'if the meaning is not understood' (rtogs, 'to understand'): ma ... na. skyes te, 'arise, and'. mi gcig gis, 'by one person, by someone'. 'di ltar yin gyi ngo sprad pas, 'because he points out (that) it is like this': gyi is here read as gyis or as marking the words pointed out; the other recension has gyis. mtshang rigs te, 'seeing the hidden thing' (mtshang, 'what is concealed, a flaw'), where the other recension has mtshang rig ste: rigs is the print's spelling of rig, 'to see, to know'. 'jigs pa bral ba, 'free of fear', without the dang that bral usually takes, which the other recension has. 'dra bar, 'like, in the same way', runs on to the next sentence. The print runs mi and gcig together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: འདིར་ ཡང་ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ གི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ སྐུ་ ཆེ་ ལ་ ཡན་ལག་ རིག་པ༔ ནམ་མཁའི་ ཁམས་ དང་ མཉམ་པར་ ཆར་བའི་ ཚེ༔ ངེས་པར་ དངངས་སྐྲག་ སྐྱེས་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: Here also, blood-drinkers' deity-host, body great and limbs coarse(?), sky's expanse with equal-ly dawning's time-at, certainly terror-fright arises, and:
sentences.i: here too, when the host of blood-drinking deities dawns, their bodies huge, their limbs massive(?), as vast as the expanse of the sky, terror and fright are sure to arise.
sentences.n: sku che la, 'the body great and', with la joining two descriptions. yan lag, 'limb'. rig pa is doubtful ([?]) and does not fit: the image shows a vowel sign over the ra and no sa, but the sense wants rags pa, 'coarse, gross, massive', which the other recension has. rig pa may be a misprint for rags pa; it is kept as printed, and the translation follows the sense of rags pa, with a query. nam mkha'i khams, 'the realm of the sky, space'. mnyam par, 'equally, as much as'. char ba'i tshe, 'at the time of dawning': char is read as the print's spelling of 'char, 'to dawn', which the other recension has; tshe, 'time, when'. nges par, 'certainly'.

sentences.w: ངོ་སྤྲོད་ འདི་ ཐོབ་ མ་ཐག་ཏུ་ རང་སྣང་ངམ༔ ཡི་དམ་དུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ ནས་ སྔར་ གོང་དུ་ བླ་མས་ གདམས་པའི་ འོད་གསལ་ མ་ དང༔ ཕྱིས་ ཤར་བའི་ རང་བྱུང་ གི་ འོད་གསལ་ གཉིས་ མ་བུ་ འཕྲད་ དེ༔
sentences.l: Face-introduction this obtained as-soon-as, self-appearance-or yidam-as face-knowing, then: before earlier-at lama-by instructed's clear-light mother and; later dawned's self-arisen's clear-light, two, mother-child meet, and:
sentences.i: But as soon as one receives this pointing out, one knows them as one's own appearance or as the yidam, and the two meet as mother and child: the clear light the lama taught before, the mother, and the self-arisen clear light that dawns now.
sentences.n: thob ma thag tu, 'as soon as (it) is obtained'. rang snang ngam, 'self-appearance or': -am, 'or', takes the last letter of the word before it (ngam after -ng). sngar gong du, 'before, earlier', two words for one thing. bla is doubtful ([?]): bla mas gdams pa'i, 'that the lama instructed', with bla ma and -s, 'by'; the other recension has sngar goms pa'i, 'that one has grown used to before', in place of gong du bla mas gdams pa'i. 'od gsal ma, 'the mother clear light', the clear light of reality, known in practice; phyis shar ba'i rang byung gi 'od gsal, 'the self-arisen clear light that dawns later', the child, met now in the bardo (shar, the past of 'char; rang byung, 'arising of itself'). ma bu, 'mother and child', as in the parts before. 'phrad de, 'meet, and' ('phrad, 'to meet'); the other recension has 'dres te, 'mingle'.

sentences.w: རང་ ལ་ རང་ཤར་ རང་གྲོལ་དུ་ སྔར་ འདྲིས་ ཀྱི་ མི་ དང་ འཕྲད་བ་ ལྟར་ རང་རིག་ རང་གསལ་དུ་ རང་གྲོལ་ལོ༔
sentences.l: Oneself-to, self-dawned, self-freed-as, before acquainted's person with meeting like, self-knowing self-clear-as self-freed.
sentences.i: Dawning of itself in oneself and freed of itself, like meeting a person one knew before, it is freed of itself, aware of itself and clear of itself.
sentences.n: rang la rang shar, 'dawned of itself in oneself'; rang grol, 'freed of itself, natural liberation', the words of the cycle's title. sngar 'dris kyi mi dang 'phrad ba ltar, 'like meeting a person one knew before', as in 009; 'phrad ba is the print's spelling of 'phrad pa. rang rig, 'self-knowing'; rang gsal, 'self-clear, luminous of itself'. rang grol lo closes the sentence with the sentence-ending -o after -l; the other recension has rang rig rang gsal rang grol du 'gyur ro, 'becomes self-knowing, self-clear and self-freed'.

sentences.w: འདིའི་ ངོ་སྤྲོད་ མ་ ཐོབ་ ན༔ གང་ཟག་ བཟང་པོ་ ཉམས་ ཀྱང་ འདི་ ནས་ ཕྱིར་ ལོག་ སྟེ་ འཁོར་བར་ འཁྱམས་མོ༔
sentences.l: This's face-introduction not obtained if: person good experience(?) though, here from back turned, and, saṃsāra-in wanders.
sentences.i: If one does not receive this pointing out, even a good person with experience(?) turns back from here and wanders in saṃsāra.
sentences.n: ma thob na, 'if (one) does not obtain': ma ... na. 'di'i ngo sprod, 'the pointing out of this'; the other recension has 'dis, 'by this'. gang zag bzang po, 'a good person'; bzang po is doubtful on the image ([?]), though the other recension has it. nyams kyang is obscure: nyams is 'meditative experience', and also 'to decline, to fail'; it is read, as a guess, 'even if (he) has experience' or 'even if (he) is good in experience'. The other recension has yin kyang, 'even if he is (a good person)', which is the plain sense. phyir log ste, 'turns back, and' (log, the past stem of ldog, 'to turn back'). 'khyams mo, 'wanders', with the sentence-ending -o after -m.

sentences.w: དེ་ནས་ གའུ་རི་ བརྒྱད་ ཀྱི་ ཁྲོ་མོ་ དང༔ ཕྲ་མེན་མ་ མགོ་བརྙན་ སྣ་ཚོགས་པ་ རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ ནང་ ནས་ ཐོན་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Then, Gaurīs eight's wrathful-women and, Phra-men-women head-likenesses various, own's brain's inside from emerged, then, oneself to dawning come.
sentences.i: Then the wrathful women, the eight Gaurīs, and the Phra men with their many kinds of heads come out from inside your own brain and dawn before you.
sentences.n: ga'u ri, Gaurī, is here written with ga'u where the rest of the part has go'u; the other recension writes ko'u rī. khro mo, 'wrathful woman' (khro, 'wrath', with the feminine -mo). phra men ma, the Phra men with the feminine -ma, as below. mgo brnyan, 'head-likeness', a head in the shape of an animal's (mgo, 'head'; brnyan, 'image, likeness'); sna tshogs pa, 'of various kinds'. nang nas, 'from within': the eight Gaurīs come from the quarters of the brain and the Phra men from round them. The print closes the sentence with 'ong ngo, where the other recension runs on with 'ong bas.

sentences.w: ཡང་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ ནི༔ ཚེ་འདས་ ཀྱི་ མིང་ ནས་ བོས་ ལ་ འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱེ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ མ་ ཡེངས་པར་ ཉོན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Again, the face-introduction, as-for: the dead-one's by-name called, and, these-words: O child-of-noble-family! Not distracted-way listen!
sentences.i: So point him out again. Call the dead person by name and say this: O child of noble family, listen without distraction.
sentences.n: The formula of the days before, with bos, the past stem of 'bod, 'to call' (see bod la above). The print runs rigs and kyi together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ ཤར་ ནས་ གོའུ་རི་མ་ དཀར་མོ་ གཡས་ ན་ ཞིང་ གི་ དབྱུག་ཏོ་ ཐོགས་པ༔ གཡོན་ ན་ བྷན་དྷ་ དམར་ གྱི་ བཀང་ ཐོགས་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ འཆར་རོ༔ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Own's brain's east from, Gaurī white, right in corpse's staff holding, left in skull-cup red with(?) filled holding, then, oneself to dawns. Her at not fear!
sentences.i: From the east of your own brain the white Gaurī, holding a corpse as a club in her right hand and in her left a skull-cup filled with red, dawns before you. Do not fear her.
sentences.n: The print does not first announce the eight Gaurīs, as the other recension does (ko rī ma mo brgyad thon nas ...), but goes straight to the first. dkar mo, 'white', with the feminine -mo; Gaurī means 'the white one'. zhing, literally 'field', is in these texts a word for a corpse; zhing gi dbyug to, 'a staff of corpse', a corpse wielded as a club, so taken from the words; the sense is not wholly sure. thogs pa, 'holding' (thogs, 'to hold, carry'). dmar gyi bkang, 'filled with red', blood: gyi stands for gyis, 'with', which the other recension has, and bkang is the past stem of 'gengs, 'to fill'. The last letter of bkang is doubtful ([?]): it stands against the frame at the start of 102.2, and is read as nga, which completes the syllable begun at the end of 102.1. The other recension has bkang ba bsnams nas. 'char ro, 'dawns'; the other recension has 'char du 'ong ngo.

sentences.w: ལྷོ་ ནས་ ཙོའུ་རི་མ་ སེར་མོ་ མདའ་གཞུ་ འགེངས་པ་ དང༔ ནུབ་ ནས་ ཕྲ་མོ་ དམར་མོ་ ཆུ་སྲིན་ རྒྱལ་མཚན་ བསྣམས་པ་ དང༔
sentences.l: South from, Caurī yellow, arrow-bow drawing, and; west from, Phra-mo(?) red, sea-monster banner holding, and;
sentences.i: from the south the yellow Caurī, drawing a bow and arrow; from the west the red Pramohā(?), holding a makara banner;
sentences.n: tso'u ri ma, Sanskrit Caurī in Tibetan letters, with -ma. mda' gzhu, 'arrow and bow'; 'gengs pa, 'filling, drawing' (a bow), the present stem of the verb whose past is bkang. dang, 'and', joins each goddess to the next to the end of the list. phra mo dmar mo: one expects a goddess's name here, and the other recension has phra men dmar mo; phra mo may be the print's form of the name, or a slip for phra men, the word the print itself uses for the class of goddesses below. It is kept as printed; the idiomatic line gives Pramohā, the name this goddess is usually given, with a query. chu srin, 'water monster', the makara, a sea creature like a crocodile; chu srin rgyal mtshan, 'a makara banner', a victory banner with a makara on it; the other recension has chu srin gyi rgyal mtshan.

sentences.w: བྱང་ ནས་ བེ་ཏ་ལི་ ནག་མོ་ རྡོ་རྗེ་ དང་ བྷནྡྷ་ དམར་ གྱིས་ བཀང་བ་ བསྣམས་པ་ དང༔ ཤར་ལྷོ་ ནས་ པུ་ཀ་སི་ དམར་སེར་ གཡས་པས་ རྒྱུ་མ་ བཟུང་ ནས་ གཡོན་པས་ ཞལ་དུ་ གསོལ་བ་ དང༔
sentences.l: North from, Vetālī black, vajra and skull-cup red-with filled holding, and; south-east from, Pukkasī red-yellow, right-by intestines seized, then, left-by mouth-to eating, and;
sentences.i: from the north the black Vetālī, holding a vajra and a skull-cup filled with red; from the south-east the red-yellow Pukkasī, holding entrails in her right hand and eating them with her left;
sentences.n: be ta li, Sanskrit Vetālī in Tibetan letters; be is doubtful on the image ([?]), though the other recension has be ta lī. nag mo, 'black'. rdo rje dang bhandha, 'a vajra and a skull-cup'. pu ka si, Pukkasī, written in the other recension pusk+a sī. shar lho, 'south-east' (shar, 'east'; lho, 'south'): the next four come from the four intermediate quarters. rgyu ma, 'intestines'. bzung nas, 'having seized' (bzung, the past stem of 'dzin, 'to hold'). zhal du gsol ba, 'putting to the mouth, eating': gsol is the respectful word for eating, used of the deities; the other recension closes the phrase without dang.

sentences.w: ལྷོ་ནུབ་ ནས་ གསྨ་རི་ ལྗང་ནག་ གཡོན་ ན་ བྷནྡྷ་ ཁྲག་ གིས་ བཀང་བ་ བཟུང་ ནས་ གཡས་པའི་ རྡོ་རྗེས་ དཀྲུགས་ ཅིང་ ཉམས་པའི་ ཆུ་ ལ་ གྲིས་ ཞལ་དུ་ གསོལ་བ་ དང༔
sentences.l: South-west from, Ghasmarī dark-green, left in skull-cup blood-with filled seized, then, right's vajra-by stirred, and, [nyams-pa's water at gris(?)] mouth-to drinking, and;
sentences.i: from the south-west the dark green Ghasmarī, holding in her left hand a skull-cup filled with blood, stirring it with the vajra in her right and drinking it (... ?);
sentences.n: gsma ri is doubtful ([?]): the first stack is read gsma, where the other recension has kasma rī; the name is Ghasmarī. khrag gis bkang ba, 'filled with blood'. g.yas pa'i rdo rjes, 'with the vajra of the right (hand)': rdo rje with -s, 'by'. dkrugs cing, 'stirring, and': dkrugs is the past stem of dkrug, 'to stir, to churn'; the other recension has dkrug. The words after it, nyams pa'i chu la gris, are obscure, and both nyams and chu are doubtful on the image ([?]); the editor looked at them again at four times enlargement and kept the reading with its marks. Word by word they give 'with a knife(?) at the water of the spoiled(?)': nyams pa, 'spoiled, broken'; chu, 'water'; gris, perhaps gri, 'knife', with -s, 'by'. None of this fits the sentence, and the sense of the phrase is uncertain; the idiomatic line leaves it out. The other recension has only dkrug cing zhal du gsol ba, 'stirs it and drinks'. The print uses zhal du gsol ba, 'puts to the mouth', for drinking as for eating.

sentences.w: ནུབ་བྱང་ ནས་ ཙཎྜ་ལི་ སེར་སྐྱ་ མགོ་ ལུས་ ཕྲག་པ་ བཀལ་ ཏེ་ གཡས་པས་ ཙིཏྟ་ བསྣམས་ ནས་ གཡོན་པས་ ལུས་པོ་ ཟ་བ་ དང༔
sentences.l: North-west from, Caṇḍālī pale-yellow, head body shoulder loaded, and, right-by heart held, then, left-by body eating, and;
sentences.i: from the north-west the pale yellow Caṇḍālī, carrying a head and a body on her shoulder(?), holding a heart in her right hand and eating the body with her left;
sentences.n: tsaN+Da li, Sanskrit Caṇḍālī in Tibetan letters; tsaN+Da is doubtful on the image ([?]); the other recension writes tsan dha lī. ser skya, 'pale yellow' (ser, 'yellow'; skya, 'pale, whitish'). mgo lus phrag pa bkal te, 'loading head and body on the shoulder, and': phrag pa, 'shoulder', without la, 'on'; bkal, the past stem of 'gel, 'to load'. bkal is doubtful on the image ([?]), and the other recension has mgo lus phral ba, 'tearing the head from the body', as the print itself says of Śmaśānī next; the print's reading is kept and the sense marked as not sure. tsit ta, Sanskrit citta, 'mind', here as in the other recension the heart, the organ. lus po, 'body', the corpse; za ba, 'eating'.

sentences.w: བྱང་ཤར་ ནས་ སྨེ་ཤ་ནི་ མཐིང་ནག་ མགོ་ ལུས་ ཕྲལ་ ནས་ ཟ་བ་ དང༔
sentences.l: North-east from, Śmaśānī dark-blue, head body torn-apart, then, eating, and;
sentences.i: from the north-east the dark blue Śmaśānī, tearing a head from a body and eating it;
sentences.n: sme sha ni, Sanskrit Śmaśānī, 'she of the charnel ground', in Tibetan letters; the other recension writes sme sha nī. mgo lus phral nas, 'having torn the head and body apart': phral, the past stem of 'phral, 'to separate, to tear apart'. The other recension has zhing gi mgo lus, 'the head and body of a corpse'.

sentences.w: གནས་ ཀྱི་ གོའུ་རི་ མ་མོ་ བརྒྱད་པོ་ ཡང་ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ ཡབ་ ལྔ་ ལ་ བསྐོར་ ནས་ རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ ནང་ ནས་ ཐོན་ ནས་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Places' Gaurī mother-goddesses eight-all also blood-drinking fathers five to surrounded, then, own's brain's inside from emerged, then, dawning come. Them at not fear!
sentences.i: These eight Gaurī mother-goddesses of the sacred places, too, surrounding the five blood-drinking fathers, come out from inside your own brain and dawn. Do not fear them.
sentences.n: gnas kyi, 'of the places', the sacred sites of the tantras, to which the Gaurīs belong, as the Phra men below belong to the yul, 'lands'. go'u ri ma mo: ma mo, 'mother', is the name of a class of fierce goddesses (Sanskrit mātṛkā); the other recension has ko'u rī ma brgyad po here and ko rī ma mo brgyad above. brgyad po, 'all eight' (-po after a number gathers the whole set). yab lnga, 'the five fathers', the five blood-drinkers of days eight to twelve. bskor nas, 'having surrounded' (bskor, the past stem of skor, 'to surround'). The print runs 'ong and ngo together across the line join, here divided, and writes a tsheg before the ༔ (ངོ་༔).

sentences.w: ཀྱེ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ དེའི་ ཕྱི་རིམ་ ནས་ ཡུལ་ གྱི་ ཕྲ་མེན་མ་ བརྒྱད་ ཐོན་ ནས་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! That's outer-ring from, lands' Phra-men-women eight emerged, then, dawning come.
sentences.i: O child of noble family, from the ring outside them the eight Phra men of the lands come out and dawn.
sentences.n: de'i phyi rim, 'its outer ring' (phyi, 'outer'; rim, 'tier, ring'): the Phra men stand in a ring outside the Gaurīs. yul gyi, 'of the lands, of the countries'. The print has no ma yengs par nyon cig, 'listen without distraction', which the other recension has here, and no rang la, 'to you'. From here on, each Phra men's name is a Sanskrit name in Tibetan letters ending in mu kha (Sanskrit mukhā, 'faced'), followed by her colour and the Tibetan word for her animal's head: mu kha is the print's spelling of mu ka throughout, which the other recension has.

sentences.w: ཤར་ ནས་ སེང་ཧ་ སྨུག་ནག་ སེང་ མགོ་མ༔ ལག་ གཉིས་ བྲང་ཁར་ བསྣོལ་ ནས་ ཁའི་ ནང་དུ་ རོ་ ཐོགས་ རལ་པ་ བསིགས་པ་ དང༔
sentences.l: East from, Siṃha dark-maroon, lion head-woman; hands two chest-at crossed, then, mouth's inside-in corpse holding, mane shaking(?), and;
sentences.i: From the east, the dark maroon Siṃhamukhā, lion-headed, her two hands crossed on her chest, a corpse in her mouth, tossing her mane(?);
sentences.n: seng ha, Sanskrit siṃha, 'lion', without the mu kha that the other recension has (seng ha mu ka) and that the print has for all the other seven: the name is Siṃhamukhā, 'Lion-Faced'. seng mgo ma, 'lion-headed one' (seng, short for seng ge, 'lion'; mgo, 'head'; -ma, feminine); the other recension has seng mgo can, with can, 'having'. brang khar, 'on the chest' (brang kha, 'chest', with -r). bsnol nas, 'having crossed' (bsnol, the past stem of snol, 'to cross, interlace'). kha'i nang du, 'inside the mouth'. ro, 'corpse'; thogs, 'holding'. ral pa, 'mane, locks of hair'. bsigs pa is taken as 'shaking, tossing'; the sense is not sure. The other recension has ro thogs te, 'holds a corpse, and'.

sentences.w: ལྷོ་ ནས་ བྱ་ཀྲི་མུ་ཁ་ དམར་མོ་ སྟག་ མགོ་མ༔ ལག་ གཉིས་ བསྣོལ་ ནས་ མིག་འབྲུ་ ཚུགས་སུ་ བལྟ་ ཞིང་ མཆེ་བ་ གཉེར་པ་ དང༔
sentences.l: South from, Vyāghrīmukhā red, tiger head-woman; hands two crossed, then, eyeballs fixed-ly gazing and, fangs baring, and;
sentences.i: from the south, the red Vyāghrīmukhā, tiger-headed, her two hands crossed, staring with fixed eyes and baring her fangs;
sentences.n: bya kri mu kha, Sanskrit Vyāghrīmukhā, 'Tiger-Faced', in Tibetan letters. stag, 'tiger'. The other recension has lag gnyis mthur du bsnol, 'hands crossed downward'. mig 'bru, 'eyeball' (mig, 'eye'; 'bru, 'grain'). tshugs su blta, 'to gaze fixedly' (tshugs, 'set, planted'): blta is the future stem of lta, 'to look', where the other recension has lta. mche ba gnyer pa, 'wrinkling (the lips over) the fangs, baring the fangs' (gnyer, 'wrinkle, snarl').

sentences.w: ནུབ་ ནས་ སྲི་ལ་མུ་ཁ་ ཝ་ མགོ་ཅན༔ གཡས་པས་ རྒྱུ་མ་ བཟུང་ ཞིང་ སྤུ་གྲི་ ཐོགས་ ནས་ གཡོན་པས་ རྒྱུ་མ་ ཟ་བ་ དང༔ ཁྲག་ ལྡག་པ་ དང༔
sentences.l: West from, Śṛgālamukhā, fox head-having; right-by intestines seized and, razor holding, then, left-by intestines eating, and; blood licking, and;
sentences.i: from the west, Śṛgālamukhā, fox-headed, holding entrails and a razor in her right hand and eating entrails with her left, and licking blood;
sentences.n: sri la mu kha, Sanskrit Śṛgālamukhā, 'Jackal-Faced', in Tibetan letters. wa, 'fox'; mgo can, 'having a head (of)'. Here the print gives no colour (the other recension has nag mo, 'black'), and has the entrails and the razor both in the right hand, where the other recension has the razor in the right and the entrails in the left. spu gri, 'razor' (spu, 'hair'; gri, 'knife'). ldag pa, 'licking'. The two dang, 'and', make the licking a second phrase of the same goddess.

sentences.w: བྱང་ ནས་ ཤྭ་ན་མུ་ཁ་ མཐིང་ནག་ སྤྱང་ མགོ་ཅན༔ ལག་པ་ གཉིས་ ཀྱི་ རོ་ ཁ་ ཁྱེ་ ནས་ མིག་འབྲུ་ ཚུགས་སུ་ བལྟ་བ་ དང༔
sentences.l: North from, Śvānamukhā dark-blue, wolf head-having; hands two by(?) corpse mouth khye(?), then, eyeballs fixed-ly gazing, and;
sentences.i: from the north, the dark blue Śvānamukhā, wolf-headed, carrying a corpse to her mouth(?) with her two hands, staring with fixed eyes;
sentences.n: shwa na mu kha, Sanskrit Śvānamukhā, 'Dog-Faced', in Tibetan letters. spyang, short for spyang ki, 'wolf'. lag pa gnyis kyi, 'of the two hands', where 'by' is meant: kyi stands for kyis, which the other recension has. ro kha khye is kept as printed and is not clear: the other recension has ro khar khyer, 'carries a corpse to the mouth', and the print's kha khye may be that phrase without its two final ra; ro kha could also be 'the corpse's mouth'. The translation follows the other recension's sense, with a query. tshugs su blta ba, 'staring fixedly', as above; the other recension has tshigs su lta ba.

sentences.w: ཤར་ལྷོ་ ནས་ ཀྲི་ཏ་མུ་ཁ་ དཀར་སེར་ བྱ་རྒོད་ མགོ་ཅན༔ ཞིང་ཆེན་ ཕྲག་ ལ་ ཁུར་ ནས་ ཀེང་རུས་ ལག་ཏུ་ ཐོགས་པ་ དང༔
sentences.l: South-east from, Gṛdhramukhā white-yellow, vulture head-having; great-corpse shoulder on carried, then, skeleton hand-in holding, and;
sentences.i: from the south-east, the whitish yellow Gṛdhramukhā, vulture-headed, carrying a corpse on her shoulder and holding a skeleton in her hand;
sentences.n: kri ta mu kha, Sanskrit Gṛdhramukhā, 'Vulture-Faced', in Tibetan letters (kri ta for gṛdhra). dkar ser, 'white-yellow'. bya rgod, 'vulture' (bya, 'bird'; rgod, 'wild'). zhing chen, 'great field', a human corpse, as zhing above. phrag la khur nas, 'carrying on the shoulder' (khur, 'to carry on the back or shoulder'). keng rus, 'skeleton'. lag tu, 'in the hand'.

sentences.w: ལྷོ་ནུབ་ ནས་ ཀ་ཀ་མུ་ཁ་ དམར་ནག་ དུར་བྱའི་ མགོ་ཅན༔ ཞིང་ཆེན་ ཕྲག་ ལ་ ཁུར་བ་ དང༔
sentences.l: South-west from, Kaṅkamukhā dark-red, charnel-bird's head-having; great-corpse shoulder on carrying, and;
sentences.i: from the south-west, the dark red Kaṅkamukhā, with the head of a charnel-ground bird, carrying a corpse on her shoulder;
sentences.n: ka ka mu kha, Sanskrit Kaṅkamukhā, 'Heron-Faced', where the other recension writes kang ka mu ka; the print has ka ka for kaṅka and mu kha for mu ka, its own spellings, and the name is easily confused with that of Kākamukhā, the next. dur bya, 'charnel-ground bird' (dur, 'grave, charnel ground'; bya, 'bird'), a carrion bird; dur bya'i mgo can, 'having the head of a charnel bird'.

sentences.w: ནུབ་བྱང་ ནས་ ཁ་ཁ་མུ་ཁ་ ནག་མོ་ བྱ་རོག་ གི་ མགོ་ཅན༔ གཡོན་དུ་ བྷནྡྷ་ ཐོགས་ ནས༔ གཡས་པས་ རལ་གྲི་ ཐོགས་ ཏེ་ གློ་སྙིང་ ཟ་བ་ དང༔
sentences.l: North-west from, Kākamukhā black, crow's head-having; left-in skull-cup holding, then, right-by sword holding, and, lungs-heart eating, and;
sentences.i: from the north-west, the black Kākamukhā, crow-headed, holding a skull-cup in her left hand and a sword in her right, eating lungs and heart;
sentences.n: kha kha mu kha, Sanskrit Kākamukhā, 'Crow-Faced', in Tibetan letters; the other recension writes kha khā mu ka. bya rog, 'crow, raven'. g.yon du, 'in the left'. glo snying, 'lungs and heart' (glo, 'lung'; snying, 'heart'). The print runs du and bhandha together, and bhandha and thogs across the line join; both are divided here.

sentences.w: བྱང་ཤར་ ནས་ ཧུ་ལུ་མུ་ཁ་ མཐིང་ན་ འུག་པའི་ མགོ་ཅན༔ གཡས་སུ་ རྡོ་རྗེ་ ཐོགས་ ཤིང་ གཡོན་དུ་ རལ་གྲི་ བསྣམས་ ཤིང་ ཤ་ ཟ་བ་ དང༔
sentences.l: North-east from, Ulūkamukhā dark(?)-blue, owl's head-having; right-in vajra holding and, left-in sword holding and, flesh eating, and;
sentences.i: from the north-east, the dark blue(?) Ulūkamukhā, owl-headed, holding a vajra in her right hand and a sword in her left, eating flesh.
sentences.n: hu lu mu kha, Sanskrit Ulūkamukhā, 'Owl-Faced', in Tibetan letters. mthing na: na is doubtful on the image ([?]); the other recension has mthing nag, 'dark blue', the colour the print gives Śvānamukhā above, and mthing na is read as that. 'ug pa, 'owl'. thogs shing, bsnams shing, 'holding, and'. sha, 'flesh, meat'. The other recension has the vajra in the right hand, but in the left a conch from which she drinks blood (g.yon pas dung khrag 'thung ba); the print has a sword in the left hand, and eating flesh.

sentences.w: ཡུལ་ གྱི་ ཕྲ་མེན་མ་ བརྒྱད་པོ་ ཡང་ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ ཡབ་ ལྔ་ ལ་ བསྐོར་ ནས་ རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ ནང་ ནས་ ཐོན་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ ཤར་ འོང་ངོ༔ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔ གང་ ཤར་ ཐམས་ཅད་ རང་སྣང་ རིག་པའི་ རྩལ་དུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Lands' Phra-men-women eight-all also blood-drinking fathers five to surrounded, then, own's brain's inside from emerged, then, oneself to dawned come. Them at not fear! Whatever dawned all, self-appearance, knowing's energy-as face-knowing do!
sentences.i: These eight Phra men of the lands, too, surrounding the five blood-drinking fathers, come out from inside your own brain and dawn before you. Do not fear them. Whatever dawns, recognise it all as your own appearance, the energy of awareness.
sentences.n: As for the Gaurīs above. shar 'ong ngo, 'come dawning': the print writes 'ong ngo contracted, as one syllable ('ongo), written out here as on the other pages; shar, the past of 'char, stands where the print elsewhere has 'char du. gang shar thams cad, 'all whatever dawns'. rig pa'i rtsal du, 'as the energy of awareness'; the other recension has rig pa'i ngang du, 'in the state of awareness'.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ སྒོ་མ་ བཞི་ ཡང་ རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ ནང་ ནས་ ཐོན་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Gate-women four also own's brain's inside from emerged, then, oneself to dawning come. Face-knowing do!
sentences.i: O child of noble family, the four gatekeepers, too, come out from inside your own brain and dawn before you. Recognise them.
sentences.n: kyai, written with the doubled vowel sign as in the pilot. sgo ma, 'gate-woman', the female gatekeeper (sgo, 'gate'): one stands at each of the four gates of the maṇḍala. The other recension has 'ong bas, 'because they come', running on to ngo shes par gyis shig.

sentences.w: རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ ཤར་ ནས་ སྟག་གདོང་ དཀར་མོ་ ལྕགས་ཀྱུ་མ༔ གཡོན་པས་ བྷན་དྷ་ དམར་ གྱིས་ བཀང་ ནས་ ཐོགས་པ་ གཅིག་ཏུ་ ཤར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Own's brain's east from, Tiger-Faced white, Iron-Hook-Lady; left-by skull-cup red-with filled, then, holding, one-as(?) dawning comes.
sentences.i: From the east of your own brain the white tiger-faced Aṅkuśā, the Iron-Hook Lady, holding in her left hand a skull-cup filled with red, comes and dawns.
sentences.n: stag gdong, 'tiger-faced' (stag, 'tiger'; gdong, 'face'). lcags kyu ma, 'Iron-Hook Lady' (lcags kyu, 'iron hook', with -ma), the gatekeeper Aṅkuśā, as in 006, named for the hook she holds there; here she holds no hook. Here the print differs from the other recension, which has rta gdong, 'horse-faced', and lcags kyu 'dzin pa, 'holding a hook'; the print gives her a skull-cup filled with blood. bkang is doubtful ([?]); it is written with a tsheg before nas, as usual. thogs pa gcig tu, 'holding, as one(?)': gcig tu, 'as one, together, in one'; the sense is not sure, and the idiomatic line leaves it out. shar du 'ong ngo, 'comes to dawn' (shar, the past of 'char, with -du). The print runs gi and klad together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: ལྷོ་ ནས་ ཕག་གདོང་ སེར་མོ་ ཞགས་པ་ འཛིན་པ༔ ནུབ་ ནས་ སེང་གདོང་ དམར་མོ་ ལྕགས་སྒྲོག་ འཛིན་པ་ དང༔ བྱང་ ནས་ སྦྲུལ་གདོང་མ་ ལྗང་མོ་ དྲིལ་བུ་ འཛིན་པ་ དང༔
sentences.l: South from, Sow-Faced yellow, noose holding; west from, Lion-Faced red, iron-chain holding, and; north from, Snake-Faced-Woman green, bell holding, and;
sentences.i: From the south the yellow sow-faced one, holding a noose; from the west the red lion-faced one, holding an iron chain; from the north the green snake-faced one, holding a bell;
sentences.n: phag, 'pig, sow'; zhags pa, 'noose'; she is the gatekeeper Pāśā, the Noose Lady. seng gdong, 'lion-faced'; lcags sgrog, 'iron chain' (Śṛṅkhalā, the Chain Lady). sbrul gdong ma, 'snake-faced one' (sbrul, 'snake'; -ma, feminine), where the other recension writes sprul gdong ma; ljang mo, 'green'; dril bu, 'bell' (Ghaṇṭā, the Bell Lady). 'dzin pa, 'holding' ('dzin, 'to hold'). The other recension has phag gdong ma and seng gdong ma, with -ma, and ljang khu, 'green'. The print runs dril and bu together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: སྒོ་མ་ བཞི་ ཡང་ རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ ནང་ ནས་ ཐོན་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔ ཡི་དམ་ གྱི་ ལྷ་ ཡིན་པས་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Gate-women four also own's brain's inside from emerged, then, oneself to dawning come. Yidam's deities are-because, face-knowing do!
sentences.i: These four gatekeepers, too, come out from inside your own brain and dawn before you. They are deities of your yidam: recognise them.
sentences.n: The sentence that announced the gatekeepers is said again to close them. yi dam gyi lha yin pas, 'because they are deities of the yidam', as in 009 and 010.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ཧེ་རུ་ཀ་ དྲག་པོའི་ ལྷ་ སུམ་ཅུའི་ ཕྱི་རིམ་དུ་ དབང་ཕྱུག་མ་ ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་བརྒྱད་ མགོ་བརྙན་ སྣ་ཚོགས་ དང་ བཅས་ཏེ༔ མཚོན་ཆ་ སྣ་ཚོགས་ ཐོགས་ ནས་ རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ ནང་ ནས་ ཐོན་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Heruka fierce's deities thirty's outer-ring-in, Īśvarīs twenty-and-eight, head-likenesses various with together, and: weapons various holding, then, own's brain's inside from emerged, then, oneself to dawning come.
sentences.i: O child of noble family, in the ring outside the thirty deities of the fierce heruka, the twenty-eight Īśvarīs, with heads of every kind and holding every kind of weapon, come out from inside your own brain and dawn before you.
sentences.n: The print has དང་ཕྱུག་མ (dang phyug ma), a misprint for དབང་ཕྱུག་མ (dbang phyug ma), corrected here. There is no ba even at ten times enlargement, but only 'Lady', Īśvarī, gives sense, and the other recension has dbang phyug ma. he ru ka drag po'i lha sum cu, 'the thirty deities of the fierce heruka': the five blood-drinkers with their five consorts, the eight Gaurīs, the eight Phra men and the four gatekeepers make thirty; the other recension has sum cu tham pa, 'thirty in all'. sum cu'i, 'of the thirty', with -'i after the vowel. phyi rim du, 'in the outer ring'. nyi shu rtsa brgyad, 'twenty-eight': nyi shu, 'twenty', and rtsa, which joins the units to the tens, brgyad, 'eight'. dang bcas te, 'together with'. mtshon cha, 'weapon'; sna tshogs, 'of every kind'.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔ གང་ ཤར་ ཐམས་ཅད་ རང་སྣང་ རིག་པའི་ རང་རྩལ་དུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔ དོན་ཆེན་ འགག་ ལ་ ཐུགས་པའི་ དུས་ཚོད་ འདིར༔ བླ་མའི་ གདམས་ངག་ དྲན་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Them at not fear! Whatever dawned all, self-appearance, knowing's own-energy-as face-knowing do! Great-matter crucial-point at reaching(?)'s time this-at, lama's instruction remembering do!
sentences.i: Do not fear them. Whatever dawns, recognise it all as your own appearance, the natural energy of awareness. At this moment, when the great matter has come to its crucial point, remember the lama's instruction.
sentences.n: rang rtsal, 'own energy, natural play' (rang, 'self'; rtsal, 'energy'). The other recension has de la ma 'jigs par, 'without fearing them', running on. don chen, 'the great matter'; 'gag, 'crucial point', literally a narrow pass. thugs pa'i is the print's reading, as in 003, where the sense wants thug pa'i, 'of reaching', in the set phrase 'gag la thug pa, 'to come to the crucial point', which the other recension has ('gags la thug pa'i); thugs is 'mind' in the respectful register and gives no sense here. It is kept as printed. dus tshod 'dir, 'at this time'. dran par gyis shig, 'remember!' (dran, 'to remember'). The print runs pa'i and rang together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ཤར་ ནས་ སྲིན་མོ་ སྨུག་ནག་ གཡག་ མགོ་མ༔ ལག་ ན་ ཐོད་པ་ ཐོགས་པ་ དང༔ ཚངས་མ་ དམར་སེར་ སྦྲུལ་ མགོ་མ༔ ལག་ ན་ པདྨ་ བསྣམས་པ་ དང༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! East from, Ogress dark-maroon, yak head-woman, hand in skull holding, and; Brahmā-Lady red-yellow, snake head-woman, hand in lotus holding, and;
sentences.i: O child of noble family, from the east: the dark maroon Rākṣasī, yak-headed, holding a skull in her hand; the red-yellow Brahmāṇī, snake-headed, holding a lotus;
sentences.n: The Īśvarīs come six to a quarter, each with an animal's head and something in her hand; the print here begins at once with the six of the east. srin mo, 'ogress' (Sanskrit rākṣasī). g.yag, 'yak'. lag na, 'in the hand'. thod pa, 'skull', where the other recension has rdo rje, 'vajra'. tshangs ma, 'Brahmā's lady', Brahmāṇī (tshangs pa, 'Brahmā', with -ma), where the other recension writes tshangs pa. sbrul, 'snake'. padma, 'lotus', where the other recension has 'khor lo, 'wheel'.

sentences.w: ལྷ་ཆེན་ དཀར་ལྗང་ གཟིག་ མགོ་མ༔ ལག་ ན་ ཏྲི་ཤུལ་ ཐོགས་པ་ དང༔ གཏོགས་འདོད་ སྔོན་མོ་ སྲེ་མོང་ མགོ༔ ལག་ ན་ འཁོར་ལོ་ འཛིན་པ་ དང༔
sentences.l: Great-God('s-lady) white-green, leopard head-woman, hand in trident holding, and; Gtogs-'dod blue, mongoose head, hand in wheel holding, and;
sentences.i: the white-green Mahādevī, leopard-headed, holding a trident; the blue Gtogs 'dod, mongoose-headed, holding a wheel;
sentences.n: lha chen, 'the great god', Mahādeva, that is Śiva; here his goddess, Mahādevī, as tshangs ma is Brahmā's. dkar ljang, 'white-green', where the other recension has ljang nag, 'dark green'. gzig, 'leopard'. tri shul, 'trident'. gtogs 'dod is not explained: gtogs is 'to belong to, to touch' and 'dod 'to desire', and the name is given as it stands. sngon mo, 'blue'. sre mong, 'weasel, mongoose'; mgo, 'head', here without -ma. 'khor lo, 'wheel'.

sentences.w: གཞོན་ནུ་ དམར་མོ་ དྲེད་ ཀྱི་ མགོ༔ ལག་ ན་ མདུང་ཐུང་ འཛིན་པ་ དང༔ བརྒྱ་བྱིན་ དཀར་མོ་ དོམ་ མགོ་མ༔ ལག་ ན་ རྒྱུ་ཞགས་ ཐོགས་པ་ དང༔
sentences.l: Youth red, brown-bear's head, hand in short-spear holding, and; Hundred-Offerings white, bear head-woman, hand in intestine-noose holding, and;
sentences.i: the red Kaumārī, with the head of a brown bear, holding a short spear; the white Indrāṇī, bear-headed, holding a noose of entrails;
sentences.n: gzhon nu, 'youth', Kumāra, the young war god; here his goddess, Kaumārī. dred, 'brown bear'; dred kyi mgo, 'the head of a brown bear', where the other recension has dred mgo ma. mdung thung, 'short spear' (mdung, 'spear'; thung, 'short'). brgya byin, 'Hundred Offerings', the Tibetan name of Indra; here his goddess, Indrāṇī. dom, 'bear', the black bear. rgyu zhags, 'noose of intestines' (rgyu, short for rgyu ma; zhags, 'noose').

sentences.w: ཤར་ གྱི་ རྣལ་འབྱོར་མ་ དྲུག་ རང་ གི་ ཀླད་པའི་ ནང་ ནས་ ཐོན་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: East's yoginīs six own's brain's inside from emerged, then, oneself to dawning come. Them at not fear!
sentences.i: These six yoginīs of the east come out from inside your own brain and dawn before you. Do not fear them.
sentences.n: rnal 'byor ma, 'yoginī', the feminine of rnal 'byor pa, 'yogin': the Īśvarīs are also called yoginīs. The other recension has klad pa'i nang nas, without rang gi, and 'char ro. The next part begins on the next line, with the six of the south: kyai rigs kyi bu, lho nas.
